questions.questionText: Which factor of production involves risk-taking?
What is the basic problem facing all economies?

options.text: how to achieve a stable balance of payments

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows the production possibility curve (PPC) for an economy.
capital goods
consumer goods
What will happen to the opportunity cost of producing more units of consumer goods in terms of
capital goods as the economy moves down its PPC from point X to point Z?

options.text: It will decrease continuously from point X to point Z.
It will decrease up to point Y and then increase towards point Z.
It will increase continuously from point X to point Z.
It will increase up to point Y and then decrease towards point Z.

questions.questionText:
An economy operates entirely as a market system.
Which type of service would not be provided in such an economy?

The diagram shows the equilibrium market price P and quantity Q for rice in a country.
E E
price
O Q
quantity
Which government action could cause the market price for rice to become P ?

options.text: encouraging the export of rice from the country
imposing a maximum price below the market price for rice
providing a subsidy to farmers to produce more rice

questions.questionText:
A major highway has been built at a cost of US$175 million between Nairobi, Kenya and its
suburbs. This reduces travel time and increases safety, but there are environmental problems for
small enterprises along its route.
Who bears the external costs of this project?

options.text: the authorities who paid for the highway
the commuters who travel to work in Nairobi
the construction companies that built the highway
the small enterprises along the route

questions.questionText: What is a function of a central bank?
What is most likely to increase the total output of a firm in the short run?

options.text: a rise in the length of the working day
a rise in the number of days holiday
a rise in the school leaving age

questions.questionText:
What will make it harder for a trade union to increase the wage rate for its members, without
reducing employment?

options.text: a switch from short-term to long-term fixed contracts of employment
an increase in the number of substitutes for the product
growth in an economy and increased demand for labour
lower price elasticity of demand for the product

questions.questionText: What is likely to assist a government’s policy of reducing inflation?

options.text: allowing businesses to borrow money for longer periods
encouraging the public to spend more money
increasing lending to members of the public
raising the interest rate on credit card borrowing

questions.questionText: Which international market is closest to the model of perfect competition?
Which form of production would be least likely to have the advantages of economies of scale?

The table shows a firm’s average revenue and average cost at different levels of output.
When all output is sold, which level of output gives maximum profit?
output average average
(units) revenue (US$) cost (US$)
Which statement about total fixed cost is correct?

options.text: It is calculated by adding total cost and total variable cost.
It is calculated by dividing total cost by output.
It must be paid even if output is zero.

questions.questionText: What is a disadvantage of direct taxes?

options.text: They can be a disincentive to work.
They can be based on people’s ability to pay.
They can be a major source of tax revenue.

questions.questionText: When is a government said to balance its budget?

options.text: when all goods and services are taxed equally
when economic growth is the same in all regions of the economy
when its total income equals its total expenditure
when total exports equal total imports

questions.questionText:
In which case is success for the government in achieving the first aim likely to cause problems in
achieving the second?
first aim second aim

options.text: price stability stable balance of payments
stable balance of payments more even distribution of income

growth?
What is used to measure inflation?

was followed by the loss of jobs resulting from the regular downturn in global economic activity.
Which types of unemployment occurred?
first type of second type of

Iran has recently experienced a natural increase in population.
What is the most likely cause of this increase?

options.text: The birth rate exceeded the death rate.
The death rate exceeded the birth rate.

questions.questionText:

Which combination of indicators is most likely to represent a developed country?
size of primary sector birth rate literacy rate
(% of GDP) (births per 1000) (% of population)

Developing countries are sometimes given aid by charities and foreign governments.
Which aid programme would be least likely to lead to long-term economic growth?

options.text: the building of an irrigation system
the construction of a new airport
the distribution of gifts of food

questions.questionText: What is a valid economic argument in favour of trade protection?

What is most likely to happen if South Korea builds a factory in Switzerland that becomes
profitable?

options.text: South Korea’s imports of goods will decrease.
South Korea’s investment income will increase.
Switzerland’s trade balance in goods will worsen.
Switzerland’s trade balance in services will improve.

questions.questionText: Which government policy is most likely to improve a country’s balance of trade?

options.text: a decrease in the exchange rate
a decrease in the level of tariffs
